panels.description: Count of selected HPAs whose current replicas are greater than or equal to maxReplicas. This is not node utilization or cluster capacity.
panels.title: HPAs at Max (count)

panels.description: Current replicas as a percentage of the configured HPA maximum. 100% means the HPA is at its replica ceiling; it does not mean the node is full.
panels.title: HPA Replica Saturation

panels.description: How many additional replicas each HPA can still add before reaching maxReplicas.
panels.title: HPA Replica Headroom

panels.description: Desired minus current replicas. Positive values show that the workload has not yet caught up with the HPA decision; negative values show scale-down in progress.
panels.title: HPA Reconciliation Gap

panels.description: The CPU utilization observed by the HPA compared with its configured CPU target. This is the signal that drives the current CPU-only HPA.
panels.title: HPA CPU Signal: Current vs Target

panels.description: HPA controller conditions. A persistent ScalingLimited=1 together with rising latency indicates that min/max or another policy is constraining scaling.
panels.title: HPA Controller Conditions (true = 1)

panels.description: Available deployment replicas as a percentage of desired replicas. Values below 100% indicate rollout, readiness, crash, or scheduling lag.
panels.title: Deployment Availability

panels.description: Per-pod CPU usage divided by configured CPU requests. This is closer to the percentage used by CPU-based HPA than raw node CPU.

targets.expr: 100 * sum by (namespace, pod) (rate(container_cpu_usage_seconds_total{job="kubernetes-nodes-cadvisor",namespace=~"$namespace",pod=~"(${deployment:regex})-.*",container!="",image!=""}[$__rate_interval])) / clamp_min(sum by (namespace, pod) (kube_pod_container_resource_requests{namespace=~"$namespace",pod=~"(${deployment:regex})-.*",resource="cpu",unit="core"}), 0.001)

panels.title: Pod CPU / Requests

panels.description: Per-pod working-set memory divided by memory requests. High values identify pods with insufficient requests even when nodes still have free memory.

targets.expr: 100 * sum by (namespace, pod) (container_memory_working_set_bytes{job="kubernetes-nodes-cadvisor",namespace=~"$namespace",pod=~"(${deployment:regex})-.*",container!="",image!=""}) / clamp_min(sum by (namespace, pod) (kube_pod_container_resource_requests{namespace=~"$namespace",pod=~"(${deployment:regex})-.*",resource="memory",unit="byte"}), 1)

panels.title: Pod Memory / Requests

panels.description: Percentage of container CPU scheduling periods that were throttled. High throttling can increase latency even when node CPU appears free.

targets.expr: 100 * sum by (namespace, pod) (rate(container_cpu_cfs_throttled_periods_total{job="kubernetes-nodes-cadvisor",namespace=~"$namespace",pod=~"(${deployment:regex})-.*",container!="",container!="POD",image!=""}[$__rate_interval])) / clamp_min(sum by (namespace, pod) (rate(container_cpu_cfs_periods_total{job="kubernetes-nodes-cadvisor",namespace=~"$namespace",pod=~"(${deployment:regex})-.*",container!="",container!="POD",image!=""}[$__rate_interval])), 0.001)

panels.title: Pod CPU Throttling

panels.description: Total CPU requests from all namespaces divided by node allocatable CPU. This is scheduler pressure, not actual CPU usage.

targets.expr: 100 * sum by (node) (kube_pod_container_resource_requests{resource="cpu",unit="core"} * on (namespace, pod) group_left(node) kube_pod_info{node=~"$node"}) / on (node) kube_node_status_allocatable{resource="cpu",unit="core",node=~"$node"}

panels.title: Node CPU Requests / Allocatable

panels.description: Total memory requests from all namespaces divided by node allocatable memory. This shows whether the scheduler has room for more replicas.

targets.expr: 100 * sum by (node) (kube_pod_container_resource_requests{resource="memory",unit="byte"} * on (namespace, pod) group_left(node) kube_pod_info{node=~"$node"}) / on (node) kube_node_status_allocatable{resource="memory",unit="byte",node=~"$node"}

panels.title: Node Memory Requests / Allocatable

panels.description: Nodes currently managed by Karpenter. Correlate changes here with HPA scale-out and pending pods.
panels.title: Karpenter-managed Nodes

panels.description: Pods that Karpenter currently considers unschedulable. A non-zero value is the trigger side of node provisioning.
panels.title: Karpenter Unschedulable Pods

panels.description: Cloud-provider errors observed by Karpenter over the last five minutes. Non-zero values explain failed NodeClaim provisioning.
panels.title: Karpenter Cloud Errors

panels.description: p95 time from an unschedulable pod entering provisioning until it becomes bound. This measures node scale-out latency visible to workloads.
panels.title: Pod Provisioning p95

panels.description: NodeClaims created and terminated per second by NodePool. Simultaneous high rates indicate churn or aggressive consolidation.
panels.title: NodeClaim Churn by NodePool

panels.description: NodePool CPU, memory, and pod usage reported by Karpenter. Use the dedicated Karpenter dashboard for full NodePool analysis.
panels.title: NodePool Resource Usage

description: Kubernetes workload scaling diagnostics: HPA decisions, replica ceilings, rollout readiness, pod resource pressure, CPU throttling, and scheduler headroom.
title: Kubernetes Scaling - Pods & Nodes
